newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat surges, ends higher as fund buys late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat surges, ends higher as fund buys late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher amid a late surge sparked by fund buying in the March contract, traders said.

March was buoyed throughout the session by mill-related buying. Those gains were extended as Rosenthal Collins, a commission house with large fund interests, bought two million March bushels after stops were hit toward the close.

"(Rosenthal's buying) had to be technically-related. We also saw professional buying in the July on the close that threw the (CBOT/KCBT July) spread out of line by a couple of cents," a floor trader said.

New crop July and September had been lower throughout the session amid forecasts for snow and rain Thursday and Friday in the southern and central U.S. Plains, which might prove beneficial to the wheat. But those contracts drew support from the late rally and ended higher.
KCBT wheat settled one to 9-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 9-1/4 at $4.15-1/2, its highest close since last Wednesday. July gained 3-1/2 cents to close at $3.54-1/2.

In addition to Rosenthal's late buying, Cargill Investor Services bought close to one million March in similar technical buying on the close. In all, CIS bought 1.9 million March Wednesday, traders said.
